evals.prompt: I want a game like Crossy Road where we hop across a busy road on our phones. We'll all be at my house on the same Wi-Fi. First one across wins.
evals.expected_output: The first grill round asks in one message whether anyone will play on a phone and how they should move, offering swipe (one hop or step) versus a little stick (keep moving), together with the other game questions. The skill does not scaffold or write game.js until they confirm a four-or-five-sentence replay. After that confirm, the project is scaffolded with --render=3d and --transport=local. Then Research, Look, and Flow briefs run in parallel (or as four separate passes if the host cannot launch subagents), and a Programming pass writes only game.js. game.js sets input.touch to 'swipe', keeps keyboard working, and does not raise TICK_HZ or edit core/ for smoothness or mobile input.

evals.prompt: Ok that's the game, go build it. Use helpers / subagents if you can.
